implementation_notes: The Observable module ships the structure: mix it in, add_observer(obj, :update) subscribes, notify_observers(*args) broadcasts to every observer, and delete_observer/delete_observers unsubscribe; it was stdlib until Ruby 3.0 and now lives in the observer gem. The manual fallback is an Array of procs or objects that publish() iterates - which is what small objects usually use - while dry-events and similar gems package the same registry with thread safety.
code_sketch:
require 'observer'

class OrderChannel
  include Observable
  def publish(order)
    changed                     # notify_observers is a no-op without it
    notify_observers(order)     # each observer's #update receives it
  end
end
# channel.add_observer(Billing.new); channel.delete_observer(billing)
pitfalls: notify_observers silently does nothing unless changed (or changed(true)) was called first - observers then report stale state with no error.
add_observer stores the observer in a hash as a strong reference; observers are never collected until delete_observer is called.
Observable's registry is not thread-safe: concurrent add_observer/notify_observers needs an external Mutex.
